content: Methyl ergonovine is classified as an ergot alkaloid medication. It is prescribed to prevent or treat uterine bleeding that may occur following childbirth or an abortion. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Methyl ergonovine is available in tablet form and is taken orally three to four times a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions or do not understand the directions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take the medication exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed by your doctor. Before taking methyl ergonovine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to methyl ergonovine, other ergot alkaloids (such as Cafergot, Ergostat, or Bellergal), or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially other ergot alkaloids and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of high blood pressure, or if you have or have had any blood vessel, heart, kidney, or liver diseases. Additionally, inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking methyl ergonovine, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Methyl ergonovine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following minor side effects, especially if they are severe or persistent: upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, or a bad taste in your mouth. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: seizures, chest pain, rapid heartbeat, difficulty breathing, dizziness, ringing in the ears, leg cramps, or a skin rash. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from light, excessive heat, and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing the prescribed course of methyl ergonovine, contact your doctor.
